headline_marked: Viral audio: [[Cantonment OC withdrawn]] over comments on Hasina's return
headline: Viral audio: Cantonment OC withdrawn over comments on Hasina's return
summary: Officer-in-Charge Md. Rakibul Hasan was removed from his post after an audio clip surfaced where he allegedly criticized the government and police force.
details: The Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Cantonment Police Station, Md. Rakibul Hasan, has been withdrawn from his post following the viral spread of a controversial audio clip on social media.
According to Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) sources, the voice in the audio has been preliminarily identified as that of Rakibul Hasan.
In the recording, the speaker claims that former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina is returning in December and asserts that the police force would be unable to do anything to stop it.
The audio also contains allegations regarding the political affiliations of senior police officials and claims that crores of taka were exchanged for the appointment to the OC position.
Following these developments, Rakibul Hasan has been attached to the DMP headquarters.
The DMP is continuing its investigation into the matter to verify the claims made in the audio clip.
caption:
A Cantonment Police OC has been withdrawn after a viral audio clip surfaced claiming Sheikh Hasina would return in December.

The Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Cantonment Police Station, Md. Rakibul Hasan, has been withdrawn from his post following the viral spread of a controversial audio clip on social media.

According to Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) sources, the voice in the audio has been preliminarily identified as that of Rakibul Hasan.

In the recording, the speaker claims that former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina is returning in December and asserts that the police force would be unable to do anything to stop it.

The audio also contains allegations regarding the political affiliations of senior police officials and claims that crores of taka were exchanged for the appointment to the OC position.

Following these developments, Rakibul Hasan has been attached to the DMP headquarters.

The DMP is continuing its investigation into the matter to verify the claims made in the audio clip.

#Bangladesh #Dhaka #Police #BreakingNews #DMP

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV

headline: 1,484 hospitalised as 5 more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: The total death toll for the year has reached 176, according to the Health Emergency Operation Center and Control Room of the DGHS.
details: Five people died of dengue in the last 24 hours, according to a regular bulletin from the Health Emergency Operation Center and Control Room of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
During the same period, 1,484 dengue patients were admitted to various hospitals across the country.
The distribution of admissions includes 227 in Dhaka South City Corporation, 207 in Dhaka North City Corporation, and 190 in Dhaka division outside the city corporations.
Other regions reported significant numbers: 252 in Khulna, 211 in Barishal, 192 in Chattogram, 102 in Rajshahi, 64 in Mymensingh, 35 in Rangpur, and 4 in Sylhet.
The DGHS reports that the total number of dengue deaths this year has now reached 176.
caption:
5 more deaths and 1,484 hospitalisations in just 24 hours. The dengue crisis continues to escalate.

Five people died of dengue in the last 24 hours, according to a regular bulletin from the Health Emergency Operation Center and Control Room of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

During the same period, 1,484 dengue patients were admitted to various hospitals across the country.

The distribution of admissions includes 227 in Dhaka South City Corporation, 207 in Dhaka North City Corporation, and 190 in Dhaka division outside the city corporations.

Other regions reported significant numbers: 252 in Khulna, 211 in Barishal, 192 in Chattogram, 102 in Rajshahi, 64 in Mymensingh, 35 in Rangpur, and 4 in Sylhet.

The DGHS reports that the total number of dengue deaths this year has now reached 176.

#Bangladesh #Dengue #HealthCrisis #DGHS #PublicHealth

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star
